title: Hybrid edge steering: latency SLIs, geo-pin heuristics, and burst-aware load shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a hybrid edge steering policy that combines latency-based routing, geo pinning, and capacity-aware steering. The goal is to keep user-visible P95 latency under the target SLO across regions while minimizing cross-region egress and avoiding cascading overloads via circuit breakers and graceful shedding.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes a policy that accepts latency thresholds, geo-pin weights, and capacity-signal thresholds
Canary traffic for hybrid steering available in staging and results in <5% cross-region pinning changes compared to baseline
Automated circuit breaker triggers when regional spare capacity < configured threshold; automatic fallback to nearest healthy region occurs with documented TTL
Load shedding policy drops low-priority requests first (embeddings pre-warm) and returns structured 429 with retry-after and hint headers
Monitoring dashboards show SLI (P50/P95/P99) by region, cross-region egress, shed-rate, and circuit-breaker activations
Runbook and cleanup scripts exist for manual blackout and rollback
notes: Background: Recent incidents where a single-region spike caused cross-region flapping and elevated tail latencies. Current steering uses simple latency-first with no capacity awareness.
Goal is to reduce unnecessary egress while protecting SLOs and making shedding observable and debuggable.
Trade-offs: strict geo pinning reduces egress but can increase latency during regional degradation; too-aggressive shedding hurts customer experience for low-latency interactive endpoints.
We will prototype as a policy library that the router can evaluate at request-time using recent windowed signals (10s latency buckets, 1m capacity estimates).
decisions: Use hybrid scoring: score(region) = alpha * normalized_latency + beta * normalized_capacity_utilization + gamma * geo_preference_score
Default alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1 for public hosted routes. Values tunable per-customer for Dedicated.
Pinning heuristic: if user's last 3 successful requests were served in same region and that region's health score > 0.75, prefer pin with soft-ttl 5m
Circuit breaker window: 30s evaluation over 1m sliding window. Trip when error_rate > 5% OR available_capacity < 15%
Load shedding bands: L0 (no shed), L1 (best-effort) shed 10% of low-priority jobs, L2 shed 50%, L3 emergency full shed for non-critical batch/async
Return structured 429 with headers: X-Redwood-Shed-Level, Retry-After, X-Redwood-Hint-Region
